attempted_claim: Do there exist universal constants C_1, C_2 > 0 such that for every n >= 1 and every centrally symmetric convex body K in R^n there exists a centrally symmetric convex body T in R^n with Banach-Mazur distance d_BM(K,T) <= C_1 and with Poincare constant C_P(lambda_{\bar T}) <= C_2, where lambda_T is the uniform probability measure on T and \bar T := Cov(lambda_T)^{-1/2} T is its isotropic renormalization? Prove or disprove.
decisive_failure: The target is an isomorphic form of the KLS conjecture; four concrete routes (direct T=K, symmetric localization, M-ellipsoid upgrade, BM-stability transfer) were each blocked with explicit Theta(sqrt(n)) and exp(Theta(n)) losses, and no original increment or auditable adjacent alternative emerged. No claim is made beyond this documented blockage.
